passages.text: Now when the people saw that Moses was delayed in coming down from the mountain, they gathered around Aaron and said, “Come, make us gods who will go before us. As for this Moses who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him!”
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel waited for Moses.
Moses was on Mount Sinai.
Moses did not come down quickly.
The people saw that Moses was delayed.
The people gathered together.
They gathered around Aaron.
Aaron was Moses’ brother.
Aaron was with the people.
The people spoke to Aaron.
They said, “Get up.
Make gods for us.
These gods will go before us.
Moses brought us out of Egypt.
We do not know what happened to Moses.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֣רְא הָעָ֔ם כִּֽי־ בֹשֵׁ֥שׁ מֹשֶׁ֖ה לָרֶ֣דֶת מִן־ הָהָ֑ר וַיִּקָּהֵ֨ל הָעָ֜ם עַֽל־ אַהֲרֹ֗ן וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ אֵלָיו֙ ק֣וּם׀ עֲשֵׂה־ לָ֣נוּ אֱלֹהִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר יֵֽלְכוּ֙ לְפָנֵ֔ינוּ כִּי־ זֶ֣ה׀ מֹשֶׁ֣ה הָאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הֶֽעֱלָ֙נוּ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם לֹ֥א יָדַ֖עְנוּ מֶה־ הָ֥יָה לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So Aaron told them, “Take off the gold earrings that are on your wives and sons and daughters, and bring them to me.”
passages.sermon:
Aaron spoke to the people.
He said, “Take off the gold earrings.
These earrings are on your wives.
They are on your sons.
They are on your daughters.
Bring the earrings to me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ אַהֲרֹ֔ן פָּֽרְקוּ֙ נִזְמֵ֣י הַזָּהָ֔ב אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּאָזְנֵ֣י נְשֵׁיכֶ֔ם בְּנֵיכֶ֖ם וּבְנֹתֵיכֶ֑ם וְהָבִ֖יאוּ אֵלָֽי׃

passages.text: Then all the people took off their gold earrings and brought them to Aaron.
passages.sermon: All the people acted together.\r\nThey removed the gold earrings from their ears.\r\nThey brought the gold earrings to Aaron.
passages.original: וַיִּתְפָּֽרְקוּ֙ כָּל־ הָעָ֔ם אֶת־ נִזְמֵ֥י הַזָּהָ֖ב אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּאָזְנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיָּבִ֖יאוּ אֶֽל־ אַהֲרֹֽן׃

passages.text: He took the gold from their hands, and with an engraving tool he fashioned it into a molten calf. And they said, “These, O Israel, are your gods, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt!”
passages.sermon:
Aaron was the brother of Moses.
Aaron was a leader of the Israelites.
Aaron took the gold from the people’s hands.
Aaron used an engraving tool.
Aaron shaped the gold.
Aaron made the gold into a calf.
The people saw the calf.
The people spoke to Israel.
The people said, “These are your gods, Israel.”
The people said, “These gods brought you out of Egypt.”
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֣ח מִיָּדָ֗ם וַיָּ֤צַר אֹתוֹ֙ בַּחֶ֔רֶט וַֽיַּעֲשֵׂ֖הוּ עֵ֣גֶל מַסֵּכָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֵ֤לֶּה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶעֱל֖וּךָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: When Aaron saw this, he built an altar before the calf and proclaimed: “Tomorrow shall be a feast to the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
Aaron was the brother of Moses.
Aaron saw the golden calf.
Aaron built an altar in front of the calf.
Aaron called out to the people.
Aaron said, “Tomorrow will be a feast to the LORD.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֣רְא אַהֲרֹ֔ן וַיִּ֥בֶן מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לְפָנָ֑יו וַיִּקְרָ֤א אַֽהֲרֹן֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר חַ֥ג לַיהוָ֖ה מָחָֽר׃

passages.text: So the next day they arose, offered burnt offerings, and presented peace offerings. And the people sat down to eat and drink, and got up to indulge in revelry.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel made a golden calf.
They believed this calf was their god.
The next day, the people woke up early.
They brought burnt offerings to the calf.
They also brought peace offerings to it.
After this, the people sat down.
They ate food.
They drank.
Then they got up.
They began to celebrate wildly.
They acted in a way that showed disrespect to God.
passages.original: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֙ימוּ֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וַיַּעֲל֣וּ עֹלֹ֔ת וַיַּגִּ֖שׁוּ שְׁלָמִ֑ים וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב הָעָם֙ לֶֽאֱכֹ֣ל וְשָׁת֔וֹ וַיָּקֻ֖מוּ לְצַחֵֽק׃פ

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go down at once, for your people, whom you brought up out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD said, “Go down at once.
Your people have corrupted themselves.
You brought these people up from the land of Egypt.”
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֑ה לֶךְ־ רֵ֕ד כִּ֚י שִׁחֵ֣ת עַמְּךָ֔ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶעֱלֵ֖יתָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: How quickly they have turned aside from the way that I commanded them! They have made for themselves a molten calf and have bowed down to it. They have sacrificed to it and said, ‘These, O Israel, are your gods, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.’ ”
passages.sermon:
God spoke about the people of Israel.
God said they turned aside quickly from His commands.
God gave them a way to follow.
They did not stay on that way.
They made a calf from melted metal for themselves.
They bowed down to the calf.
They offered sacrifices to the calf.
They said to Israel, “These are your gods.”
They said, “These gods brought you out of the land of Egypt.”
passages.original: סָ֣רוּ מַהֵ֗ר מִן־ הַדֶּ֙רֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֔ם עָשׂ֣וּ לָהֶ֔ם עֵ֖גֶל מַסֵּכָ֑ה וַיִּשְׁתַּֽחֲווּ־ לוֹ֙ וַיִּזְבְּחוּ־ ל֔וֹ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֵ֤לֶּה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶֽעֱל֖וּךָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: The LORD also said to Moses, “I have seen this people, and they are indeed a stiff-necked people.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD said, “I have seen these people.
These people are the Israelites.
They are stubborn.
They refuse to listen.
They do not obey easily.
They are a stiff-necked people.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֑ה רָאִ֙יתִי֙ אֶת־ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה עַם־ קְשֵׁה־ עֹ֖רֶף הֽוּא׃

passages.text: Now leave Me alone, so that My anger may burn against them and consume them. Then I will make you into a great nation.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God said, “Leave Me alone now.
I am very angry with the people of Israel.
I will let My anger burn against them.
I will destroy them completely.
After that, I will make you, Moses, into a great nation.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּה֙ הַנִּ֣יחָה לִּ֔י וְיִֽחַר־ אַפִּ֥י בָהֶ֖ם וַאֲכַלֵּ֑ם וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂ֥ה אוֹתְךָ֖ לְג֥וֹי גָּדֽוֹל׃

passages.text: But Moses sought the favor of the LORD his God, saying, “O LORD, why does Your anger burn against Your people, whom You brought out of the land of Egypt with great power and a mighty hand?
passages.sermon:
Moses was a prophet and leader of Israel.
The LORD is God.
Moses spoke to the LORD his God.
Moses tried to find favor with the LORD.
Moses said, “O LORD, why does Your anger burn against Your people?
You brought these people out of Egypt.
You used great power.
You used a mighty hand.”
passages.original: וַיְחַ֣ל מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֶת־ פְּנֵ֖י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑יו וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לָמָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ יֶחֱרֶ֤ה אַפְּךָ֙ בְּעַמֶּ֔ךָ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הוֹצֵ֙אתָ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּכֹ֥חַ גָּד֖וֹל וּבְיָ֥ד חֲזָקָֽה׃

passages.text: Why should the Egyptians declare, ‘He brought them out with evil intent, to kill them in the mountains and wipe them from the face of the earth’? Turn from Your fierce anger and relent from doing harm to Your people.
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to the LORD.
Moses referred to the Israelites as God's people.
Moses said, "Why should the Egyptians speak this way?"
The Egyptians might say, "God brought the Israelites out with evil intent."
The Egyptians might say, "God wanted to kill them in the mountains."
The Egyptians might say, "God wanted to wipe them from the face of the earth."
Moses asked God to turn from His fierce anger.
Moses asked God to relent from bringing harm to His people.
passages.original: לָמָּה֩ יֹאמְר֨וּ מִצְרַ֜יִם לֵאמֹ֗ר בְּרָעָ֤ה הֽוֹצִיאָם֙ לַהֲרֹ֤ג אֹתָם֙ בֶּֽהָרִ֔ים וּ֨לְכַלֹּתָ֔ם מֵעַ֖ל פְּנֵ֣י הָֽאֲדָמָ֑ה שׁ֚וּב מֵחֲר֣וֹן אַפֶּ֔ךָ וְהִנָּחֵ֥ם עַל־ הָרָעָ֖ה לְעַמֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: Remember Your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, to whom You swore by Your very self when You declared, ‘I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky, and I will give your descendants all this land that I have promised, and it shall be their inheritance forever.’ ”
passages.sermon:
God made a promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Israel.
God called them His servants.
God swore this promise by Himself.
God said, “I will make your descendants very many.
Your descendants will be as numerous as the stars in the sky.
I will give your descendants all this land I promised.
Your descendants will own this land forever.”
passages.original: זְכֹ֡ר לְאַבְרָהָם֩ לְיִצְחָ֨ק וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל עֲבָדֶ֗יךָ אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֣עְתָּ לָהֶם֮ בָּךְ֒ וַתְּדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם אַרְבֶּה֙ אֶֽת־ זַרְעֲכֶ֔ם כְּכוֹכְבֵ֖י הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְכָל־ הָאָ֨רֶץ הַזֹּ֜את אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֗רְתִּי אֶתֵּן֙ לְזַרְעֲכֶ֔ם וְנָחֲל֖וּ לְעֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: So the LORD relented from the calamity He had threatened to bring on His people.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD had threatened to bring calamity on His people.
The LORD decided not to bring this calamity.
The LORD relented.
passages.original: וַיִּנָּ֖חֶם יְהוָ֑ה עַל־ הָ֣רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֶּ֖ר לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לְעַמּֽוֹ׃פ

passages.text: Then Moses turned and went down the mountain with the two tablets of the Testimony in his hands. They were inscribed on both sides, front and back.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of Israel.
Moses turned.
Moses went down the mountain.
Moses carried the two tablets of the Testimony in his hands.
The tablets had writing on them.
The writing was on both sides of the tablets.
The writing was on the front and on the back.
passages.original: וַיִּ֜פֶן וַיֵּ֤רֶד מֹשֶׁה֙ מִן־ הָהָ֔ר וּשְׁנֵ֛י לֻחֹ֥ת הָעֵדֻ֖ת בְּיָד֑וֹ לֻחֹ֗ת כְּתֻבִים֙ מִשְּׁנֵ֣י עֶבְרֵיהֶ֔ם מִזֶּ֥ה וּמִזֶּ֖ה הֵ֥ם כְּתֻבִֽים׃

passages.text: The tablets were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, engraved on the tablets.
passages.sermon: God made the tablets.\r\nGod wrote the words on the tablets.\r\nGod engraved His writing onto the tablets.
passages.original: וְהַ֨לֻּחֹ֔ת מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים הֵ֑מָּה וְהַמִּכְתָּ֗ב מִכְתַּ֤ב אֱלֹהִים֙ ה֔וּא חָר֖וּת עַל־ הַלֻּחֹֽת׃

passages.text: When Joshua heard the sound of the people shouting, he said to Moses, “The sound of war is in the camp.”
passages.sermon:
Joshua was with Moses.
Joshua heard the people shouting.
Joshua listened carefully.
Joshua said to Moses, “I hear a sound in the camp.”
Joshua said, “It sounds like war.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֧ע יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ אֶת־ ק֥וֹל הָעָ֖ם בְּרֵעֹ֑ה וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה ק֥וֹל מִלְחָמָ֖ה בַּֽמַּחֲנֶה׃

passages.text: But Moses replied: “It is neither the cry of victory nor the cry of defeat; I hear the sound of singing!”
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to Joshua.
Moses said, “This is not the sound of victory.”
Moses said, “This is not the sound of defeat.”
Moses said, “I hear the sound of singing.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֵ֥ין קוֹל֙ עֲנ֣וֹת גְּבוּרָ֔ה וְאֵ֥ין ק֖וֹל עֲנ֣וֹת חֲלוּשָׁ֑ה ק֣וֹל עַנּ֔וֹת אָנֹכִ֖י שֹׁמֵֽעַ׃

passages.text: As Moses approached the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, he burned with anger and threw the tablets out of his hands, shattering them at the base of the mountain.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of the Israelites.
He approached the camp.
He saw the golden calf.
He saw the people dancing.
Moses became very angry.
He threw the tablets from his hands.
He broke the tablets at the base of the mountain.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר קָרַב֙ אֶל־ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וַיַּ֥רְא אֶת־ הָעֵ֖גֶל וּמְחֹלֹ֑ת וַיִּֽחַר־ אַ֣ף מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיַּשְׁלֵ֤ךְ מִיָּדוֹ אֶת־ הַלֻּחֹ֔ת וַיְשַׁבֵּ֥ר אֹתָ֖ם תַּ֥חַת הָהָֽר׃

passages.text: Then he took the calf they had made, burned it in the fire, ground it to powder, and scattered the powder over the face of the water. Then he forced the Israelites to drink it.
passages.sermon:
Moses saw the golden calf that the Israelites had made.
He took the calf.
He burned the calf in the fire.
He ground the burned calf until it became powder.
He scattered the powder over the surface of the water.
He made the Israelites drink the water with the powder.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶת־ הָעֵ֨גֶל אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשׂוּ֙ וַיִּשְׂרֹ֣ף בָּאֵ֔שׁ וַיִּטְחַ֖ן עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁר־ דָּ֑ק וַיִּ֙זֶר֙ עַל־ פְּנֵ֣י הַמַּ֔יִם וַיַּ֖שְׁקְ אֶת־ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: “What did this people do to you,” Moses asked Aaron, “that you have led them into so great a sin?”
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of Israel.
Aaron was his brother and the high priest.
The Israelites had made a golden calf and worshiped it.
Moses spoke to Aaron.
Moses said, “What did this people do to you?”
Moses asked, “Why have you brought such a great sin upon them?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶֽל־ אַהֲרֹ֔ן מֶֽה־ עָשָׂ֥ה לְךָ֖ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּֽי־ הֵבֵ֥אתָ עָלָ֖יו חֲטָאָ֥ה גְדֹלָֽה׃

passages.text: “Do not be enraged, my lord,” Aaron replied. “You yourself know that the people are intent on evil.
passages.sermon:
Aaron spoke to Moses.
Aaron said, “Do not be angry, my lord.”
Aaron said, “You know these people.”
Aaron said, “These people are bent on doing evil.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אַהֲרֹ֔ן אַל־ יִ֥חַר אַ֖ף אֲדֹנִ֑י אַתָּה֙ יָדַ֣עְתָּ אֶת־ הָעָ֔ם כִּ֥י בְרָ֖ע הֽוּא׃

passages.text: They told me, ‘Make us gods who will go before us. As for this Moses who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him!’
passages.sermon:
The people spoke to Aaron.
They said, “Make gods for us.
These gods will go before us.
Moses brought us out of Egypt.
We do not know what happened to Moses.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ לִ֔י עֲשֵׂה־ לָ֣נוּ אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֵלְכ֖וּ לְפָנֵ֑ינוּ כִּי־ זֶ֣ה׀ מֹשֶׁ֣ה הָאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הֶֽעֱלָ֙נוּ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם לֹ֥א יָדַ֖עְנוּ מֶה־ הָ֥יָה לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So I said to them, ‘Whoever has gold, let him take it off,’ and they gave it to me. And when I threw it into the fire, out came this calf!”
passages.sermon:
Aaron spoke to the people of Israel.
Aaron said, “Whoever among you has gold, take it off.”
The people removed their gold.
The people gave the gold to Aaron.
Aaron took the gold.
Aaron threw the gold into the fire.
A calf came out of the fire.
passages.original: וָאֹמַ֤ר לָהֶם֙ לְמִ֣י זָהָ֔ב הִתְפָּרָ֖קוּ וַיִּתְּנוּ־ לִ֑י וָאַשְׁלִכֵ֣הוּ בָאֵ֔שׁ וַיֵּצֵ֖א הָעֵ֥גֶל הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: Moses saw that the people were out of control, for Aaron had let them run wild and become a laughingstock to their enemies.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of the Israelites.
Moses looked at the people.
He saw that the people were out of control.
Aaron was the brother of Moses.
Aaron had let the people run wild.
The people became a laughingstock to their enemies.
passages.original: וַיַּ֤רְא מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶת־ הָעָ֔ם כִּ֥י פָרֻ֖עַ ה֑וּא כִּֽי־ פְרָעֹ֣ה אַהֲרֹ֔ן לְשִׁמְצָ֖ה בְּקָמֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: So Moses stood at the entrance to the camp and said, “Whoever is for the LORD, come to me.” And all the Levites gathered around him.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of the Israelites.
The Israelites had sinned by making a golden calf.
Moses saw the people were out of control.
Moses stood at the entrance of the camp.
He spoke to everyone.
He said, “Whoever is for the LORD, come to me.”
All the Levites came to Moses.
The Levites were one of the tribes of Israel.
They chose to stand with the LORD.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲמֹ֤ד מֹשֶׁה֙ בְּשַׁ֣עַר הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מִ֥י לַיהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י וַיֵּאָסְפ֥וּ אֵלָ֖יו כָּל־ בְּנֵ֥י לֵוִֽי׃

passages.text: He told them, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Each of you men is to fasten his sword to his side, go back and forth through the camp from gate to gate, and slay his brother, his friend, and his neighbor.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to the Levites.
He said, “The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD commands you now.
Each man must put his sword on his side.
Each man must walk through the camp.
Go from one gate to another gate.
Each man must kill his brother.
Each man must kill his friend.
Each man must kill his neighbor.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֗ם כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שִׂ֥ימוּ אִישׁ־ חַרְבּ֖וֹ עַל־ יְרֵכ֑וֹ עִבְר֨וּ וָשׁ֜וּבוּ מִשַּׁ֤עַר לָשַׁ֙עַר֙ בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וְהִרְג֧וּ אִֽישׁ־ אֶת־ אָחִ֛יו וְאִ֥ישׁ אֶת־ רֵעֵ֖הוּ וְאִ֥ישׁ אֶת־ קְרֹבֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The Levites did as Moses commanded, and that day about three thousand of the people fell dead.
passages.sermon:
The Levites obeyed Moses.
They did what Moses told them to do.
That day, about three thousand people died.
These people were from among the Israelites.
passages.original: וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֥וּ בְנֵֽי־ לֵוִ֖י כִּדְבַ֣ר מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיִּפֹּ֤ל מִן־ הָעָם֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא כִּשְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת אַלְפֵ֖י אִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: Afterward, Moses said, “Today you have been ordained for service to the LORD, since each man went against his son and his brother; so the LORD has bestowed a blessing on you this day.”
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to the Levites.
He said, "Today you have set yourselves apart for the LORD."
Each man acted against his own son and his own brother.
You obeyed the LORD, even when it was difficult.
Because of this, the LORD has given you a blessing today.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֗ה מִלְא֨וּ יֶדְכֶ֤ם הַיּוֹם֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ בִּבְנ֖וֹ וּבְאָחִ֑יו וְלָתֵ֧ת עֲלֵיכֶ֛ם הַיּ֖וֹם בְּרָכָֽה׃

passages.text: The next day Moses said to the people, “You have committed a great sin. Now I will go up to the LORD; perhaps I can make atonement for your sin.”
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of the Israelites.
The people had sinned greatly against God.
The next day, Moses spoke to the people.
Moses said, “You have committed a great sin.”
Moses said, “Now I will go up to the LORD.”
Moses said, “Perhaps I can make atonement for your sin.”
passages.original: וַיְהִי֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־ הָעָ֔ם אַתֶּ֥ם חֲטָאתֶ֖ם חֲטָאָ֣ה גְדֹלָ֑ה וְעַתָּה֙ אֶֽעֱלֶ֣ה אֶל־ יְהוָ֔ה אוּלַ֥י אֲכַפְּרָ֖ה בְּעַ֥ד חַטַּאתְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: So Moses returned to the LORD and said, “Oh, what a great sin these people have committed! They have made gods of gold for themselves.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of the Israelites.
Moses returned to the LORD.
Moses spoke to the LORD.
Moses said, “These people have sinned greatly.
They made gods of gold for themselves.”
passages.original: וַיָּ֧שָׁב מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶל־ יְהוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אָ֣נָּ֗א חָטָ֞א הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ חֲטָאָ֣ה גְדֹלָ֔ה וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י זָהָֽב׃

passages.text: Yet now, if You would only forgive their sin.... But if not, please blot me out of the book that You have written.”
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of Israel.
The people of Israel had sinned greatly.
They made a golden calf and worshiped it.
Moses spoke to the LORD.
Moses said, "Now, if You will forgive their sin, please do so."
"But if You will not forgive them, then erase my name from the book You have written."
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֖ה אִם־ תִּשָּׂ֣א חַטָּאתָ֑ם וְאִם־ אַ֕יִן מְחֵ֣נִי נָ֔א מִֽסִּפְרְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּתָֽבְתָּ׃

passages.text: The LORD replied to Moses, “Whoever has sinned against Me, I will blot out of My book.
passages.sermon: The LORD spoke to Moses.\r\nThe LORD said, “I will remove from My book anyone who sins against Me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֑ה מִ֚י אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָֽטָא־ לִ֔י אֶמְחֶ֖נּוּ מִסִּפְרִֽי׃

passages.text: Now go, lead the people to the place I described. Behold, My angel shall go before you. But on the day I settle accounts, I will punish them for their sin.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God had chosen Moses to lead the Israelites.
God had brought the Israelites out of Egypt.
God told Moses to lead the people.
God said, “Go to the place I told you about.”
God said, “I will send My angel ahead of you.”
God said, “My angel will go before you.”
God said, “One day I will judge the people.”
God said, “On that day, I will punish them for their sin.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֞ה לֵ֣ךְ׀ נְחֵ֣ה אֶת־ הָעָ֗ם אֶ֤ל אֲשֶׁר־ דִּבַּ֙רְתִּי֙ לָ֔ךְ הִנֵּ֥ה מַלְאָכִ֖י יֵלֵ֣ךְ לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וּבְי֣וֹם פָּקְדִ֔י וּפָקַדְתִּ֥י עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם חַטָּאתָֽם׃

passages.text: And the LORD sent a plague on the people because of what they had done with the calf that Aaron had made.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD sent a plague.
The LORD sent the plague on the people.
The people had sinned.
The people made a calf.
Aaron made the calf for the people.
The LORD punished the people because they made the calf.
passages.original: וַיִּגֹּ֥ף יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־ הָעָ֑ם עַ֚ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשׂ֣וּ אֶת־ הָעֵ֔גֶל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה אַהֲרֹֽן׃ס
